<break time="0.8s" /> That the plains of Texas. <break time="0.8s" /> Were pouring eastward. <break time="0.8s" /> A newly married pair. <break time="0.8s" /> Had boarded this coach. <break time="0.8s" /> At San Antonio. <break time="0.8s" /> And the mans face was reddened. <break time="0.8s" /> From many days in the wind and sun. <break time="0.8s" /> Wearing new black clothes. <break his attire. <break time="0.8s" /> The bride was not pretty. <break time="0.8s" /> Nor was she very young. <break time="0.8s" /> And she wore a dress of blue cashmere. <break time="0.8s" /> With small touches of velvet. <break time="0.8s" /> And many steel buttons. <break time="0.8s" /> She kept turning her head. <break time="0.8s" /> To look at her stiff, high puffed sleeves. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was quite apparent. <break time="0.8s" /> That she had cooked. <break time="0.8s" /> And expected to cook, dutifully. <break time="0.8s" /> Have you ever been in a parlor car before he asked. <break time="0.8s" /> Smiling with delight. <break time="0.8s" /> And she answered shyly. <break time="0.8s" /> That she never had. <break time="0.8s" /> He told her proudly. <break time="0.8s" /> That they would go forward to the diner later. <break time="0.8s" /> And get a big lay out. <break time="0.8s" /> The finest meal in the world. <break time="0.8s" /> For a dollar. <break time="0.8s"
